project.name: Lichii shader precompilation
project.description: Stop mid-game pipeline compilation stalls by porting switch2mac's shared pipeline key list to Lichii: a per-title, identifiers-only list of shader content hashes and fixed pipeline state, recorded during play, shareable between players, and used to build matching pipelines on background workers before the game asks for them. Includes the eviction and boot-load policy fixes the OoT profile showed are needed, and static shader discovery as the enabler for prebuilding content a player has not reached yet.

meta.origin: OoT pipeline profile of 2026-11-06 plus the azmasm/switch2mac survey.
meta.measured: OoT session 2: 1059 pipelines preloaded, 1188 built at run time, 1206 evicted, 931 evicted in one check at 169 s, 612 built in 10 s at 352 s, frames of 923/1041/1235 ms. 176 of 267 storm builds had already been built in session 1.
meta.legal: A shared list may contain shader content hashes and register state only. Never commit game shaders, SPIR-V, serialized environments, vulkan.bin, or driver blobs.
meta.naming: The on-disk list is keylist.bin next to vulkan.fork-v<N>.bin under %APPDATA%/eden/cache/shader/<title>/.

phases.title: Reconnaissance and baseline
phases.goal: Know what switch2mac actually shares, what Lichii's pipeline cache already does, and what the OoT stutter consists of. No production changes.

tasks.title: Profile OoT pipeline builds and evictions from real sessions
tasks.goal: Read two OoT sessions' logs and separate genuinely new pipelines from rebuilds of evicted ones. Record boot counts, eviction totals, storm windows, frame spikes, and unique shader counts.
success: Numbers recorded for boot preload, run-time builds, evictions and frame spikes
Known-rebuild share of a storm window measured
Cause separated into eviction churn versus new content
tasks.tests: Cross-check the per-10s ReportRuntimePipeline sums against the logged per-build lines.
tasks.changelog: OoT profile recorded: 1188 run-time builds and 1206 evictions in 11 minutes, 931 evicted in one check

tasks.title: Survey switch2mac's shared shader list
tasks.goal: Read the switch2mac README, shader_list tooling and game pages. Establish what a row contains, how rows are collected and merged, how a game build uses them, and the cost limits.
success: Row semantics, contribution flow and privacy rule written down
Dependence on locally locatable shader code identified
Build-time cost examples recorded
tasks.changelog: switch2mac shared shader list surveyed and documented

tasks.title: Enable the pipeline-diff diagnostic for one OoT session
tasks.goal: Run OoT with EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_DIFF=1 and count how many new keys share a shader set with an earlier key, and which fixed-state fields split them. This sizes the value of state-variant prefetch for OoT.
success: Count of distinct shader sets versus keys recorded
Most common differing state fields listed
Decision recorded on whether sibling prefetch is worth shipping for OoT
tasks.tests: Set EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_DIFF=1, launch OoT with EDEN_NX2_DEBUG_SERVER=127.0.0.1:6565, play 5 minutes, count 'differs in' lines.

phases.title: Per-title pipeline key list
phases.goal: A version-stable keylist.bin per title: record every built key, load shared rows, and build listed state variants on background workers as soon as their shader set is resident.

tasks.title: Design the key list format and prefetch rules
tasks.goal: Choose a binary row format (kind, key hash, shader hashes, fixed state), a normalization rule for driver id/version, dedupe by key hash, and the only safe prefetch trigger: one exact shader set already resident, with a serialized environment snapshot.
success: Format documented and versioned
Driver fields and feature-set handling decided
Thread ownership decided: builds on workers, insertion into the pipeline map on the GPU thread at TickFrame
tasks.changelog: Key list format and prefetch rules designed

tasks.title: Add the PipelineKeyList module
tasks.goal: Add src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_keylist.{h,cpp}: verified load, deterministic save, record for graphics and compute keys, shader-set index, Siblings lookup, Contains, and an EDEN_NX2_KEYLIST=0 switch. No pipeline code uses it yet.
success: Round-trip of a written file reproduces every key
Corrupt or foreign rows are dropped without touching existing rows
Driver id and version are cleared in stored rows and key hashes are stable across them
tasks.tests: New unit test in src/tests/video_core writes two graphics keys and one compute key, reloads them, compares fields, then corrupts bytes and expects a clean load.

tasks.title: Record every built pipeline into the list
tasks.goal: Record keys from the boot disk-cache loader, the runtime graphics slow path and the runtime compute path. Save the merged list next to the versioned pipeline cache at shutdown. Do not change what is built.
success: A first run over an existing cache writes about 1000 rows for OoT
Second run loads the same row count
Saving is done off the GPU thread
tasks.tests: Run OoT for a minute, count rows in keylist.bin, restart, confirm the load count logged and pipeline count at boot is unchanged.

tasks.title: Snapshot environments and prefetch listed state variants
tasks.goal: When a first-time graphics key is built, ask the list for other keys with the same six shader hashes. If any are missing, serialize the already-captured environments into a buffer and queue one worker job that deserializes them and builds each missing key with the existing CreateGraphicsPipeline path. Hand results to the GPU thread at TickFrame; never mutate the pipeline map from a worker.
success: Prefetched siblings are inserted at TickFrame and used by the draw that needs them
No build reads live Maxwell registers off the GPU thread
Per-trigger and pending caps prevent a prefetch storm
Task and mesh programs are skipped and failures are not retried
EDEN_NX2_KEYLIST_PREFETCH=0 disables it
tasks.tests: Inject a sibling state into a key list, run OoT, confirm the sibling is built on a worker and the frame that first uses it does not stall.
tasks.changelog: Key list prefetch builds listed state variants on workers from an environment snapshot

tasks.title: Verify persisted rows on a fresh pipeline cache
tasks.goal: Prove the list is independent of the versioned cache: after a CACHE_VERSION bump (or a deleted vulkan.fork-v<N>.bin), the list must still load and the runtime prefetch must rebuild matching keys from resident shaders. Record which part of the cache can and cannot be recovered offline.
success: List survives deleting the versioned cache
Recoverable versus unrecoverable rows documented
No stale row produces a wrong pipeline
tasks.tests: Move vulkan.fork-v<N>.bin aside, keep keylist.bin, boot OoT, confirm rows load and sibling prefetch still runs.

phases.title: Eviction and boot policy
phases.goal: Stop evicting pipelines the title is still working through. The profile shows eviction churn is about two thirds of OoT's mid-game build cost.

tasks.title: Replace idle-frame eviction with an LRU budget
tasks.goal: Evict only when the live pipeline count or estimated driver memory exceeds a budget, oldest use first, and never evict keys the used list says recent sessions used unless over budget. Keep an env override for A/B.
success: OoT second session no longer mass-evicts on the boot screen
Evictions and rebuilds fall well below run-time builds
Frames over 100 ms caused by known rebuilds disappear from the 352 s scenario
tasks.tests: A/B the same OoT save with EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_EVICT_BUDGET unset and set; compare erasure and rebuild lines.
tasks.changelog: Pipeline eviction is an LRU memory budget instead of a 9000-frame idle rule

tasks.title: A/B asynchronous shaders against pipeline stalls
tasks.goal: Measure Renderer.use_asynchronous_shaders=true (draws skipped while a pipeline builds) against the current blocking build on OoT. Decide whether pop-in is an acceptable trade for removed hitches.
success: Frame-time distribution compared
Visual difference described
Recommendation recorded
tasks.tests: Two OoT sessions with the same save, one setting flip; compare frames over 33 and 100 ms and screenshots.

phases.title: Static shader discovery
phases.goal: Make a shared list useful for content a player has not reached. Enumerate shader containers from the player's own title files so listed keys whose shaders are present can be built at boot, the way switch2mac's engine does.

tasks.title: Audit the title's romfs for BNSH/CGSB/SHN shader containers
tasks.goal: Use tools/nx2/extract_static_shaders.py and shader_containers.py against an extracted OoT romfs, or add a read-only path through the emulator's romfs, and report how many native programs are precompiled and how many stage/header records they carry.
success: Answer recorded: does OoT ship static shaders
If yes, count, stages and container paths listed
If no, runtime-only shader generation confirmed with evidence
tasks.tests: Run the extractor against the title dump; verify each record's extent before trusting it.
tasks.changelog: Corrected: .bphsh/.bphsc/.bphnm are Havok physics, not shaders. OoT's native programs live in 5 .bfsha (BNSH) plus agl/gsys/tera .sharcb (BAHS), agl_ndsr.pck (NDSR) and Movie/Ndve/*.dat (NDVE). All are zstd frames naming IDs 1-4.

tasks.title: Load title shader programs at boot for key-list builds
tasks.goal: Turn the extracted static set into a boot-time win. The offline sweep shows the limit: 38,801 of 39,392 programs lower, but graphics compilation needs runtime uniform values and storage pointer classifications, so static archives alone cannot build those pipelines. Use the static set to pre-lower programs into a NativeProgramKey-indexed cache, and keep the key list's recorded environments as the pipeline source for unreached content.
success: Every program the dump carries is extracted with stage, control section and native code
Pre-lowered programs are cached by NativeProgramKey and reused at first draw
Listed pipelines for unreached content are built before the first draw from key-list environments
Boot remains bounded by the used list or an explicit budget
Disabling the feature restores today's behaviour exactly
tasks.tests: Delete the title cache, boot OoT with a shared list, confirm build count and the absence of a storm in the first area.
tasks.changelog: Extracted 39,392 programs and swept them: 38,801 lower, 1,776 compile and validate with synthetic defaults, 68 refuse to lower (13 distinct opcodes). Graphics compilation needs runtime state, so pre-lowering plus key-list environments is the workable split.

tasks.title: Close the 13 lowering gaps the OoT sweep found
tasks.goal: Make the 68 programs that refuse to lower translatable. The dominant refusals are 0xabb (uniform constant load mode, 20), 0xb63 (per-tap gather proofs, 20) and 0x944 (call linkage mode, 8), then unsupported opcodes 0xc08, 0x905, 0x3a9 and 0x481 and the mode checks 0xb66, 0x243, 0x981, 0x217, 0x3c2, 0x899. Every one is reachable from FoliageShader.sharcb, agl_ndsr_vr.pck or agl_common.sharcb.
success: The offline sweep lowers all 39,392 OoT programs
Each new opcode or mode has a test with the OoT program that exposed it
No existing shader changes its lowered output
tasks.tests: Re-run sweep_static_shaders.py over the extracted OoT manifest; require zero lower-phase failures.
tasks.changelog: First gap closed: indexed ULDC (0xabb) now accepts byte and halfword widths, which unblocked all 20 compute programs that failed on it; 4 of them lower completely and the rest stop at their next instruction. Unit test covers the lowered LDC encoding for both captured instructions plus the alignment, bank, width and mode checks that must stay. Live check: Kokiri Forest renders correctly after the change. Remaining 64 programs and the exact instruction for each group are listed in learnings.md; the biggest are 0xb63 (20), 0x291 uniform LEA carry (10), 0x944 (8), and unsupported opcodes 0x905/0xc08/0x3a9/0x481 (11). Second gap closed: register-pressure operand lists for 0x811, 0xc20, 0x217/0xa17, 0x219/0xa19/0xc19, 0xc23 and 0x3c2, which used to fall through to the unsupported default whenever a high guest register forced a shadow copy. 6 of the 68 programs now lower completely; the rest are the gather proofs (20), the uniform LEA carry (10), call linkage (8), 11 unsupported opcodes and the remaining mode checks. Register-pressure drift measured and split into 1.3.4: 234 opcodes lowered, 94 described, 140 missing; a guessed fallback was rejected by the existing guard tests.

tasks.title: Give the register-pressure pass every opcode the lowering handles
tasks.goal: Close the 140-opcode gap between lower_to_maxwell.h and register_pressure.h. An opcode without an operand list is refused, which rejects the whole program the moment a high guest register forces a shadow copy; that is the "native register shadowing mode" failure in the OoT sweep.
success: The audit script reports no missing opcodes, or every remaining one is documented as deliberately unsupported
Each entry lists only the fields its own branch reads as guest registers
A wrong entry is caught by a test: a rewritten field that is not a register changes the lowered output
tasks.tests: Run tools/nx2/lower_operand_audit.py, then the [video_core] suite, then the sweep over the OoT programs that failed with native register shadowing mode.
tasks.changelog: Split out of 1.3.3 after the drift was measured: 234 opcodes lowered, 94 described. A blanket fallback for unknown opcodes was tried and reverted because the Fast Fusion and Yoshi tests guard against exactly that guess. The audit script and the per-branch method are in learnings.md.

phases.title: Sharing and collection
phases.goal: Let players exchange key lists safely, per title and per build, without ever shipping game data.

tasks.title: Split loaded rows from rows recorded this run
tasks.goal: Track which rows came from the shared list and write only new rows to a contribution file, so merging is a union of verified rows rather than a whole-file replacement.
success: Contribution file contains only rows absent from the loaded list
Merging a contribution file is idempotent
Rows are ordered deterministically for review
tasks.tests: Load a list, record one known and one new key, verify the contribution file holds exactly the new key.
tasks.changelog: PipelineKeyList tracks the hashes each Load brought in and SaveContribution writes only the rows no loaded list has (same format, sorted by key hash). A contribution is loaded back at boot as pending, so an unmerged file survives a session that adds nothing, and is removed when nothing is pending. Live A/B on OoT: with no list, contribution held all 1583 graphics + 195 compute rows; with the merged list loaded, status reported keylist_contribution 0 and no file was written. Four new unit tests cover the split, idempotent merging, the stale-file removal and a pending file surviving a session.

tasks.title: Merge tool and per-title list workflow
tasks.goal: Make per-title lists shareable. The reading side exists: tools/nx2/keylist_tool.py inspects, merges, lists programs and reports which state bytes split one shader set. Remaining: choose where a fetched list lives, how the emulator prefers it over the local one, and how a row proves it was drawn rather than only cached.
success: Two lists merge without losing or duplicating rows
A merged list loads in the emulator and builds the listed states at boot
A list can be inspected offline for stage coverage and state splits
No list carries code, a driver id or a resource, only identifiers
tasks.tests: Merge a good file, a corrupted file and a file for another title; expect success, refusal and refusal.
tasks.changelog: keylist_tool.py added (inspect/merge/programs/diff) with 12 unit tests; format and state-layout offsets measured on a real OoT list. The emulator now writes keylist.contribution.bin with only the rows no loaded list had, and merging it with keylist_tool.py is a verified union (merging OoT parked + contribution gave +0 rows and the same 319,960-byte file). Remaining: where a fetched shared list lives and how it is preferred over the local one, and how a row proves it was drawn rather than cached.

phases.title: Rollout
phases.goal: Measure the finished feature on OoT and one other title, keep the diagnostics, and ship the behaviour without experiment switches.

release.release_notes: Shader precompilation: per-title key list, sibling prefetch, budget eviction, and optional static shader discovery.

tasks.title: Measure end-to-end on OoT and one state-heavy title
tasks.goal: Record boot time, rows loaded, rows prefetched, builds and evictions per session, frames over 33/50/100 ms, and the worst frame, against the 2026-11-06 baseline.
success: Frames over 100 ms reduced and the 352 s storm gone
Boot time explained (rows built versus time)
No visual regression in screenshots
tasks.tests: Same save, same settings, two sessions per title; compare logged counters.

tasks.title: Remove experiment switches and document the shipped behaviour
tasks.goal: Keep only diagnostics that stay off unless requested. Remove the key-list experiment switch once proven, keep the prefetch cap fixed, and update the debug tooling docs.
success: No env flag decides which fix runs
Diagnostics documented in the tool table
List format and privacy rule stated in user-facing docs
tasks.tests: Grep for the experiment env names and confirm only diagnostics remain.

phases.title: Full control MCP server
phases.goal: Turn the read-only debug server into a complete MCP control surface for agents: emulator control, gamepad input, memory read/write, CPU/GPU state queries and the existing debug tools, still opt-in, loopback only, and safe for a normal run.

tasks.title: MCP control surface on the debug server
tasks.goal: Promote the existing loopback debug server from passive observation to MCP control: pause/resume, present-granular step, and a typed state snapshot. Keep it off unless EDEN_NX2_DEBUG_SERVER is set, loopback only, and one request at a time. Document the safety boundary: no file system access, no keys, no network.
success: pause, resume and step_frames work without desynchronising the Qt EmuThread
A state snapshot returns title, core state, paused flag, presents and fps
The server stays off by default and refuses non-loopback addresses
tasks.tests: Pause, step 10 presents, resume on OoT; confirm the game advances exactly 10 frames and the UI stays consistent.
tasks.changelog: pause, resume and step verified live on OoT with tools/nx2/live_check.py: presents froze at 7274 under pause, step 10 advanced exactly 10, resume cleared the paused flag, and status reported title, paused, presents, fps and caches. Unit tests: StepPresents plus the debug-server suite (11 cases, 93 assertions).

tasks.title: Gamepad and input injection over MCP
tasks.goal: Inject buttons and sticks through the emulated controller so an agent can walk to a scene, reproduce a bug, or cover an area for shader discovery without the owner playing. Timed by presents, not wall time, with a recorded sequence that can be replayed on a fresh boot.
success: Buttons and sticks are ORed over the player's mapping without changing it
Sequences replay deterministically by present count
Releasing control restores the physical controller immediately
tasks.tests: Replay a short walk in Kokiri Forest, then a second boot from the same save; both reach the same area.
tasks.changelog: Buttons and sticks, input_sequence, input_record and input_playback verified live on OoT. A three-event macro replayed twice advanced the same 73 presents both times, so the timing is present-count driven. Fixed a real bug found by the live run: recordings store buttons as hex text, and playback fed that text back through the button-name parser, so every replay threw unknown button. ParseRecordedButtons reads hex (or a number) and has a unit test. Motion and triggers are not exposed yet.

tasks.title: Guest and GPU memory read/write
tasks.goal: Read and write application memory and GPU address spaces by address and size, through Core::Memory and Tegra::MemoryManager, with unmapped ranges reported instead of guessed. Reuse the mapped-page walker already added for scan_shaders.
success: read_guest_memory and read_gpu_memory return exact bytes or a mapped-range error
write_guest_memory refuses ranges that are not mapped and reports what changed
GPU reads run on the rasterizer thread and flush caches correctly
tasks.tests: Read a known string at its process address; read a texture header at its GPU address; write and read back a scratch byte.
tasks.changelog: Guest reads verified live at 0x8000000. GPU reads needed a way to find a mapped address, so MemoryManager::FirstMappedRanges plus the gpu_memory_map tool now report the mapped ranges (the page table is not otherwise exposed). Verified live: map, read at 0x11471b3000, write of the bytes just read, and a matching read back.

tasks.title: CPU, GPU and cache state queries
tasks.goal: Expose the state an agent needs without a log round-trip: guest core register sets and thread states, active channel and GPU engine registers, pipeline and shader cache counts, frame pacing, and the existing profile zones. Extend the status tool rather than adding a second state path.
success: One call returns guest core states, active channel, pipeline cache size and eviction counters
GPU engine registers and frame pacing match the log values
Queries are read-only and cannot mutate emulator state
tasks.tests: Compare a query against the same frame's DKB trace lines and the pipeline cache log.
tasks.changelog: status.caches verified live and matches the pipeline cache counters (195 compute, 621 graphics, 1778 key-list graphics keys, 0 evictions). GPU engine registers and frame pacing comparison against DKB trace lines are still open.

tasks.title: Debug tools and shader discovery over MCP
tasks.goal: Move the remaining env-gated diagnostics behind the control surface: shader scan and dictionary extraction, frame capture options, shader inventory, reject/restore, and live toggles that are safe at a frame end. Keep the env switches as the initial value so a normal run is unchanged.
success: scan_shaders, dictionary extraction and shader inventory work over MCP
Reject and restore are reversible without a rebuild
Only diagnostics remain behind env switches; experiment switches are removed
tasks.tests: Extract the zstd dictionaries from a running OoT, decompress one bfsha and compare the BNSH count with the offline Rust scan.
tasks.changelog: shaders inventory, scan_shaders, reject_shaders and the screenshot shader toggle are implemented and verified live on OoT (57 programs at the title screen, a rejected hash changed the image and was restored afterwards). Dictionary extraction over MCP and removing the experiment switches are still open.

tasks.title: Configurable screenshot with shader and render toggles
tasks.goal: Extend the screenshot tool so an agent can compare images under controlled changes in one call: shader toggles (reject or isolate a shader, show only one stage, skip post-processing or upscaling), render overrides (resolution, sRGB/linear output, alpha), and a frame or pass selector. Return the PNG plus the state that produced it so two images are comparable.
success: screenshot accepts shader reject/isolate lists and render overrides
The response records every override that was active
Two screenshots A/B a shader or pass without a relaunch
The tool never writes outside the session dump directory
tasks.tests: Capture the same frame normally and with one shader rejected; confirm only the intended draws changed and the manifest lists the override.
tasks.changelog: screenshot save/inline verified live, and the reject A/B verified live: the response reported the override, the image differed from the plain capture, and status showed no leftover rejection. Render overrides (skipping a pass) are still open.
